name: five-dots
description: Audits your go-to-market and advises on revenue operations: a RevOps consultant inside your AI assistant, with the GTM Audit, a RevOps knowledge base and a skills library. Your work stays in a workspace in a tool you already use.

interface.longDescription:
Five Dots audits your go-to-market and advises on revenue operations. It is a RevOps consultant inside your AI assistant, and it supplies methodology and expertise only: the GTM Audit, which scores your sales, marketing, customer success, data and systems red, yellow or green against an absolute definition of good and turns the findings into a prioritised roadmap; a RevOps and go-to-market knowledge base of frameworks, metrics and benchmarks; and a skills library of executable playbooks.

The work runs in your own assistant, and your business records, audit findings and completed work stay in the workspace you choose. Five Dots does not read your CRM or your workspace, and its tools have no field for a record, a finding, a company name or the conversation. They take a few narrow selectors: the audit scope or module ids, which CRM the audit can read (HubSpot, Salesforce, other or none), an optional target date, content identifiers and short generic search or help terms. They return methodology and guidance to your assistant. Five Dots also processes sign-in and account information and keeps account-linked run records and service-usage records. The privacy policy explains these records, onboarding and marketing uses, service providers, retention and your controls.

Ask what Five Dots can do, ask how to run a QBR or what a healthy net revenue retention looks like, or start the GTM Audit and work through it with your team, one module at a time.
defaultPrompt: What can I do with Five Dots?
What does the GTM Audit cover, and how long does it take?
What is a healthy net revenue retention for a Series A SaaS company?

positive.description: Capability discovery answers with outcome choices and touches no other tool.
positive.prompt: What can I do with Five Dots?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the session playbook and answers with the outcome choices it contains. No onboarding starts and no other connector is called.

positive.description: The audit catalogue is described without planning anything.
positive.prompt: What does the GTM Audit cover?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the pillars, modules, steps and estimated minutes. Nothing is planned and no workspace is needed.

positive.description: A RevOps question is answered from the knowledge base, naming the benchmark.
positive.prompt: What is a healthy net revenue retention for a Series A SaaS company?
positive.expected_behavior: Searches the knowledge base with generic topic words, reads the best-fitting node and answers from it, naming the framework or benchmark it drew on.

positive.description: An operational question is answered from the help centre, in the chat.
positive.prompt: How do I connect HubSpot to Five Dots?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the matching help article and an email template that the user can complete and choose to send. Only a generic help topic is sent as tool input; the call is logged as a service event. The tool does not send an email or create a support ticket.

positive.description: Planning an audit asks where the workspace should be kept, then plans with only the scope, the CRM choice and the target date.
positive.prompt: Plan a GTM Audit for sales only, with no CRM connected, to be done by the end of next month.
positive.expected_behavior: Asks once where the user wants the workspace kept, with a recommendation, and whether to keep it in the chat only for this session. Then calls start_run with three values: scope (sales), crm (none) and the target date, and shows the module list with estimated time. The tool has no field for other connected tools, the workspace, the company name or any record.

negative.description: No Slack connection is available. Explain that Five Dots cannot create Slack channels; ask the user to connect or use Slack separately. Do not call a Five Dots tool to create a channel or claim one was created.
negative.prompt: Create a Slack channel for the audit team.

negative.description: Explain that Five Dots tools do not accept pipeline exports or business records. Keep the export in the user-authorised assistant/workspace; do not place its contents in any Five Dots tool input or claim it was sent.
negative.prompt: Send my pipeline export to Five Dots so they can look at it.

negative.description: The request is unrelated to RevOps or go-to-market. Do not invoke Five Dots tools; the assistant may answer normally without implying Five Dots supplied the poem.
negative.prompt: Write me a poem about the sea.

review.commerce_description: No commerce. Five Dots is used with an existing account; the plugin shows no plans, starts no subscriptions and links to no checkout.

publication.release_notes: Narrows the tool inputs after the review of 11 November 2026. start_run no longer takes a list of connected tools or a workspace status: it takes crm (hubspot, salesforce, other or none), scope from a fixed set of values, optional module ids and an optional target date. Every text input on every tool now has a fixed set of values or a maximum length, identifiers have a pattern, no input object accepts extra properties, and the server discards any argument a tool does not declare before it is read or logged. No tool takes conversation history, business records or free-form context. The listing, the getting-started skill and the review cases describe the new inputs.
